detaileddescription.para: Start with detection of "serialize" overloads, intrusive and non-intrusive.

NOTE: Detection of serializeParent and serializeThis are no longer used on "develop" in VT (eliminated with message serialization refactoring), but remain on the release branch for 1.0.0. Thus, they must stay for now.

memberdef.definition: using checkpoint::SerializableTraits< T, S >::has_serialize = detection::is_detected<serialize_t, T, S>
memberdef.name: has_serialize
nonintrustive_serialize_t

memberdef.definition: using checkpoint::SerializableTraits< T, S >::has_nonintrustive_serialize = detection::is_detected<nonintrustive_serialize_t, T, S>
memberdef.name: has_nonintrustive_serialize

memberdef.definition: using checkpoint::SerializableTraits< T, S >::has_serializeParent = detection::is_detected<serializeParent_t, T, S>
memberdef.name: has_serializeParent

memberdef.definition: using checkpoint::SerializableTraits< T, S >::has_serializeThis = detection::is_detected<serializeThis_t, T, S>
memberdef.name: has_serializeThis

detaileddescription.para: Detect byte-copyability trait and std::is_arithmetic, used for types that do not have a serialize method.
Detect different types of re-constructibility: default constructors, explicitly tagged constructors for serializers, and reconstruct methods.

memberdef.definition: using checkpoint::SerializableTraits< T, S >::has_default_constructor = detection::is_detected<constructor_t, T>
memberdef.name: has_default_constructor

memberdef.definition: using checkpoint::SerializableTraits< T, S >::has_reconstruct = detection::is_detected_exact<T&, reconstruct_t, T>
memberdef.name: has_reconstruct

memberdef.type: decltype( reconstruct( std::declval< U *& >(), std::declval< void * >()))
memberdef.name: nonintrustive_reconstruct_t

memberdef.type: decltype( checkpoint::CheckpointReconstructor< U >::reconstruct( std::declval< U *& >(), std::declval< void * >()))
memberdef.name: specialized_reconstruct_t
